doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Meeting Doc Pomus
summary: He met Doc Pomus at the Baby Grand, visited his home, and Doc's Billboard letter went unknown to him.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Do you know – tell me about – because this is an important character in the new phase of your career – tell me when you first met Doc Pomus, the great . . .
At the Baby Grand. The funniest thing, he had a metal brace . . .
This is Doc Pomus, the great blues composer and singer.
Right, and writer. Anyway, Doc used to come to the Baby Grand.

Anyhow, he was sitting in the chair, and this brace was reflecting light. He would move his foot or something, and the lights would reflect. I kept seeing this. Then I realized, that’s that thing on his leg. That’s how we met, because when I’d come off, I knew who he was. I go over and greet him. We sat and talked and became friends. I even was invited to his house. Ertugun – Nes Ertugun – it wasn’t Ertugun – his brother? What is it?
Oh boy. He didn’t like it, because . . .
. . . yeah. He didn’t like it, because Doc Pomus brought me to his house, and I had dinner with him. He didn’t like it. Very nasty.

The record industry, for not giving Jimmy Scott a record deal. He says, “What’s wrong with you guys? This is one of the greatest vocalists there is out there. Why don’t you give him a deal? This is crazy. He is going to die, and everybody’s going to say how great he was, and he’ll never have a deal.” Tell me your reaction. Did you read that letter in Billboard? Or did you learn about it?
So you didn’t even know that it happened.
Because you weren’t even reading Billboard then. Neither was I.
